newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand removes import quota on feed ingredients.
newsitem.headline: Thailand removes import quota on feed ingredients.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved the food policy committee's proposal to remove import quotas on animal feed raw materials such as soybeans, soymeal and fishmeal, a government official said.
The decision will be effective from November 1, she said.
The cabinet also approved a reduction in import tariffs to 10 percent from 15 percent for soymeal, to zero from five percent for soybean and to zero from three percent for corn.
The import tariff for fishmeal was kept unchanged at six percent plus a 1,400 baht/tonne ($56/tonne) surcharge.

The cabinet set a condition on corn, saying it could be imported only between February 20 and June 30 each year. The amount will be determined by the government to protect local farmers, the official said.

The approvals will change the traditional system under which the government set quotas for the amount of raw materials that could be imported under its low-tariff programme each year. Previously any imports outside such quotas faced high duties.

Feed producers had complained the previous policy was counter-productive as it made long-term planning difficult and resulted in fluctuations of local meat and poultry prices. -- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
